subject.title: feat(agents): per-agent outbound A2A allowlist override

question: Should OpenClaw accept requester-owned outbound-only per-agent A2A allowlists as the public config contract for cross-agent session tools, or require receive-side/per-capability policy before landing this PR?
rationale: The PR changes cross-agent authorization and adds public config/SDK surface, so automation cannot choose the long-term least-privilege semantics safely.

options.title: Approve outbound-only after repairs
options.body: Accept requester-owned outbound semantics, then require exact-ID normalization, changelog removal, conflict refresh, and focused validation before merge.

options.title: Require broader authorization first
options.body: Pause this branch and fold the work into bidirectional or per-capability session authorization before exposing new config.

options.title: Keep as design discussion
options.body: Leave this PR open for discussion but do not land a public config contract until broader per-agent scoping issues are settled.

recommendation.title: Approve outbound-only after repairs
recommendation.body: Accept requester-owned outbound semantics, then require exact-ID normalization, changelog removal, conflict refresh, and focused validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The path history shows repeated work on the central session visibility/A2A helper boundary and config/security semantics this PR changes.
